data.raw_text:
Philippines Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla stresses the Senate was not under attack when a "gun incident" ensued between Senate security personnel and agents of the National Bureau of Investigation. But stopped short of concluding it was staged. 

Remulla says the NBI had informed Senate maintenance  management that they were drilling and fortifying the door between the Senate building and GSIS (state insurer) following Senator Ronald Dela Rosa's call for his supporters to protect him. Dela Rosa is wanted by the International Criminal Court for crimes against humanity. 

He added the NBI agents were not wearing tactical gear and wore vests that clearly indicated they were from the NBI.

But videos show Senate security head Mao Aplasca leading his men, fully armed, to the veranda and firing the first few shots after an agent in the adjacent building identified himself as NBI. According to Remulla, an NBI agent was fired upon so he had to fire back for cover. 

More than 30 shots were fired, mostly from the Senate side.

He notes Aplasca even allowed the press to follow them to a certain point (on video as well) instead of clearing the area, despite claiming there was an attack and that they were going to make an arrest.
